payoff: Two critical PHP bugs can let a request with no login run code on your server; the fix is updating to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (21 October 2026), and php.net says no setting fully protects you.

points.title: One request
points.body: No login, no app code yet

caption:
Two critical PHP bugs can let a request with no login run code on your server.
On mod_php, php.net shows the attack can start before any application code runs (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619). The fix: update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (21 October 2026); php.net says "There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice." Source: php.net/archive/2026.php
Which version runs your server? 👇
voiceover: [fired up] Two PHP bugs let strangers run code, (break) [serious] no login needed.
[grim] A single request does it, (break) [serious] before your own code runs.
[firm] So update now. (break) [matter-of-fact] PHP says no setting fully protects you.
[confident and fast] The fixed versions are these four.
[warm, curious] Which version runs your server? (break) Check it today.

scenes.title: Security advisory
scenes.text: We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.

scenes.text: There are no complete mitigations, updating is the only safe choice.
